_doc: Operational policy facts that the BIS central-bank policy-rate series does not show, disclosed on real-time-era pages for reading the policy rows (never model inputs). Each item is shown only in editions whose last eligible day is on or after its date, the publication date of its cited source. Türkiye 2017: the BIS series is the CBRT one-week repo rate, kept at 8% all year, while the CBRT restricted funding at that rate and supplied the market at the late liquidity window lending rate. Each source fetched and checked (tcmb.gov.tr press releases and MPC decisions). The CBRT's later statement that one-week repo auctions were suspended from 12 Jan 2017 is in Inflation Report 2017-I, whose retrievable PDF was created on 1 Mar 2017; it is not cited because its publication date before the affected cutoffs cannot be shown. Türkiye 2018-2019: the late liquidity window lending rate was raised to 13.5% (25 Apr 2018) and 16.5% (23 May 2018) while the one-week repo rate stayed at 8% (tcmb.gov.tr press releases 2018-10, 2018-18); those two items and the 2017 late-liquidity-window items carry 'until' 2018-05-31 (the last day that arrangement applied) and are not shown after it; the CBRT's simplification of 28 May 2018 (one-week repo rate the funding rate again from 1 Jun 2018) and the 2019 one-week repo auction suspensions (22 Mar, 9 May) and resumptions (8 Apr, reported by ING on 18 Apr; 21 May, Reuters) are each shown from their source's own date. The resumption of 8 Apr 2019 is documented by no fetched source dated before 18 Apr, so the 2019-04-14 edition shows the suspension only. The CBRT press releases and the ING and Arab News pages were fetched and their quoted text checked. The four 2019 one-week repo auction items carry 'until' 2019-12-31: they are shown in 2019 editions only, because by the first 2020 edition the 2019 episodes had long ended (one-week repo funding at the policy rate again from 21 May 2019). Türkiye 2020: from 7 Aug 2020 the CBRT suspended one-week repo auctions and funded banks at the overnight lending rate, the late liquidity window and one-month 'traditional' repo auctions, above the one-week repo rate (backdoor tightening; no CBRT press release announced the suspension, so the earliest dated report, Anadolu Agency via Hürriyet Daily News of 7 Aug, is cited, and the CBRT's MPC summary of 27 Aug confirms it); the corridor and limit changes of 11 Aug, 18 Aug, 24 Sep, 22 Oct and 2 Nov are each shown from their source's date and carry 'until' 2020-11-19; on 19 Nov the CBRT returned all funding to the one-week repo rate from 20 Nov 2020. The CBRT's 2020 rate releases give no corridor rates, so corridor values come from ING and Reuters, checked against the CBRT's (undated) rate-history tables. The 17 Mar 2020 targeted repos below the policy rate are not recorded. Hungary 2021: the BIS series is the MNB base rate; from the tender of 18 Nov 2021 the MNB set its one-week deposit rate (weekly tenders) above it, by 40–120 bp through the last 2021 edition, and its own statements tied the tightening to that rate. Items cite the MNB's English press releases and the dated Budapest Business Journal (MTI) tender reports, each fetched and checked. The earlier, smaller spread (0.75% against a 0.60% base rate from Sep 2020 until the rates were aligned at 0.9% in Jun 2021) is not disclosed: no dated public source stating that level was retrieved.

TR.text: the CBRT lowered banks' borrowing limits at its Interbank Money Market to TL 22 billion from 11 Jan 2017 (announced 10 Jan) and to TL 11 billion from 16 Jan 2017, said funding through Borsa Istanbul repo markets 'may be limited' on days deemed necessary, and that banks could meet their remaining liquidity needs 'without limits at late liquidity window funding rate at the end of the day'; the one-week repo rate (the BIS series) stays at 8%, so it understates the CBRT's marginal funding cost from then on
TR.label: CBRT press release, 13 Jan 2017

TR.text: the MPC raised the marginal funding (overnight lending) rate from 8.5% to 9.25% and the late liquidity window lending rate from 10% to 11%, keeping the one-week repo rate at 8%
TR.label: CBRT MPC decision, 24 Jan 2017

TR.text: the MPC raised the late liquidity window lending rate from 11% to 11.75%, keeping the one-week repo rate at 8% and the overnight lending rate at 9.25%
TR.label: CBRT MPC decision, 16 Mar 2017

TR.text: the MPC raised the late liquidity window lending rate from 11.75% to 12.25%, keeping the one-week repo rate at 8% and the overnight lending rate at 9.25%
TR.label: CBRT MPC decision, 26 Apr 2017

TR.text: the MPC raised the late liquidity window lending rate from 12.25% to 12.75%, keeping the one-week repo rate at 8% and the overnight lending rate at 9.25%
TR.label: CBRT MPC decision, 14 Dec 2017

TR.text: the MPC raised the late liquidity window lending rate from 12.75% to 13.5%, keeping the one-week repo rate at 8% and the overnight lending (marginal funding) rate at 9.25%
TR.label: CBRT MPC decision, 25 Apr 2018

TR.text: the MPC raised the late liquidity window lending rate from 13.5% to 16.5% ('a strong monetary tightening'), keeping the one-week repo rate at 8% and the overnight lending rate at 9.25%
TR.label: CBRT MPC decision, 23 May 2018

TR.text: the CBRT completed the simplification of its operational framework, effective 1 Jun 2018: 'One-week repo rate will be the policy rate of the Central Bank. This rate will be equal to the current funding rate (16.50%)', with the overnight borrowing and lending rates 150 basis points below/above it; the one-week repo rate (the BIS series, 8% until then) is again the CBRT's funding rate, so its move from 8% to 16.5% on 1 Jun 2018 aligns the series with the funding cost already in force (the late liquidity window lending rate had been raised to 16.5% on 23 May 2018)
TR.label: CBRT press release, 28 May 2018

TR.text: 'Considering the developments in financial markets, it has been decided to suspend the one-week repo auctions for a period of time' (no end date given); without one-week repo funding, banks' marginal CBRT funding is the overnight lending rate (25.5%, the top of the corridor), above the 24% one-week repo rate that the BIS series shows
TR.label: CBRT press release, 22 Mar 2019

TR.text: the CBRT 'started one-week repo auctions again on 8 April, readjusting the effective cost of funding to 24%'
TR.label: ING Think, 'Turkish Central Bank to stay on hold', 18 Apr 2019

TR.text: the CBRT again decided 'to suspend the one-week repo auctions for a period of time'; bankers expected the average cost of funding to rise gradually to 25.5%, against the 24% one-week repo rate
TR.label: CBRT press release, 9 May 2019

TR.text: the CBRT 'held a repo auction for the first time in nearly two weeks, reversing a policy tightening step', injecting 17 billion lira, and lowered the lira interest rate in swap transactions to 24% from 25.5%; funding returns to the 24% one-week repo rate
TR.label: Reuters via Arab News, 'Turkish lira weakens after cenbank repos resume, FX purchase move', 21 May 2019

TR.text: the CBRT 'has also halted repo auctions and told lenders to use a 9.75 percent overnight rate instead': with one-week repo funding suspended (the CBRT's own summary of 27 Aug dates it 'as of August 7'), banks' marginal CBRT funding is the overnight lending rate (9.75%) or the late liquidity window (11.25%), above the 8.25% one-week repo rate that the BIS series shows
TR.label: Hürriyet Daily News (Anadolu Agency), 'Central Bank acts swiftly to make lira more attractive', 7 Aug 2020

TR.text: 'Liquidity limits offered to Primary Dealers in the framework of Open Market Operations (OMOs) will be reduced to zero effective from 12 August 2020' (halved from 10 Aug under the press release of 7 Aug), closing a funding channel priced below the policy rate
TR.label: CBRT press release 2020-43, 11 Aug 2020

TR.text: 'banks’ borrowing limits at the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey (CBRT) Interbank Money Market for O/N transactions will be reduced to half of their current limits effective from 19 August 2020', pushing more funding to the 11.25% late liquidity window
TR.label: CBRT press release 2020-45, 18 Aug 2020

TR.text: the MPC summary confirms that 'one-week repo auctions were suspended as of August 7; liquidity limits offered to primary dealers were first reduced to half, and then zero; banks’ borrowing limits at the CBRT Interbank Money Market for overnight transactions were reduced to half', that 'traditional repo auctions started on August 13', and that 'These steps will continue to increase the weighted average funding cost in the upcoming period'
TR.label: CBRT press release 2020-54, Summary of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting of 20 Aug 2020, 27 Aug 2020

TR.text: with the one-week repo rate raised from 8.25% to 10.25% (in the BIS series), 'the entire corridor setup has shifted upwards' with the overnight lending rate at 11.75% and the late liquidity window rate at 13.25%; one-week repo funding at the policy rate was still not provided, and ING put the effective cost of funding at 10.65%
TR.label: ING Think, 'Turkey: Outright hike instead of changing the rate corridor', 24 Sep 2020

TR.text: the MPC kept the one-week repo rate at 10.25% but 'raised the uppermost rate in its corridor, the late liquidity window (LLW), to 14.75% from 13.25%'; the 'so-called backdoor measures to rein in credit have raised the average cost of funding to 12.52% from a low of 7.34% in July'
TR.label: Reuters via Arab News, 'Turkey holds rates in surprise that sends lira to new low', 22 Oct 2020

TR.text: 'effective from 3 November 2020, banks’ borrowing limits at the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey (CBRT) Interbank Money Market will be reduced to zero', leaving the 14.75% late liquidity window as banks' marginal CBRT funding, against the 10.25% one-week repo rate
TR.label: CBRT press release 2020-65, 2 Nov 2020

TR.text: with the one-week repo rate raised from 10.25% to 15% the same day, 'starting from 20 November 2020, the funding currently provided by the Central Bank via traditional method repo auctions with one month maturity and late liquidity window facilities will instead be provided via quantity repo auctions with one-week maturity, which constitute the principal monetary policy tool'; from 20 Nov 2020 the one-week repo rate (the BIS series) is again the CBRT's funding rate
TR.label: CBRT press release 2020-69, 19 Nov 2020

HU.text: with the base rate raised from 1.80% to 2.10%, the Monetary Council said that short-term financial and commodity market risks had intensified, to which 'the Bank must respond … quickly and flexibly. The corresponding instrument for this is the one-week central bank deposit. As long as financial and commodity market risks persist, the Bank must be ready to set the interest rate on one-week deposit above the base rate'; the one-week deposit rate is set at weekly tenders
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 16 November 2021

HU.text: at the tender of Thursday 18 Nov the MNB offered its one-week deposit facility at 2.5%, 40 bp over the 2.10% base rate (the BIS series)
HU.label: Budapest Business Journal (MTI), 'MNB offers 1-week depo at 2.5%, 40 bp over base rate', 19 Nov 2021

HU.text: the one-week deposit rate was raised to 2.9%, 80 bp over the base rate
HU.label: Budapest Business Journal (MTI), 'MNB raises 1-week depo rate by 40 bp to 2.9%', 25 Nov 2021

HU.text: 'The interest rate on the one-week deposit has risen above the base rate in recent weeks'; the Council did not discuss the base rate but widened the interest-rate corridor and made it asymmetrical, raising the overnight and one-week collateralised lending rates to 4.10% from 1 Dec
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 30 November 2021

HU.text: the one-week deposit rate was raised to 3.1%, 100 bp over the base rate
HU.label: Budapest Business Journal, 'MNB raises 1-week depo rate by 20 bp to 3.1%', 2 Dec 2021

HU.text: the one-week deposit rate was raised to 3.3%, 120 bp over the base rate
HU.label: Budapest Business Journal (MTI), 'MNB raises 1-week depo rate by 20 bp to 3.3%', 9 Dec 2021

HU.text: with the base rate raised from 2.10% to 2.40% and the overnight deposit rate raised to the base rate, the Council said that 'Changes to the one-week central bank deposit rate will feed into the MNB's tightening cycle for a sustained period', that the Bank 'will be ready to set the one-week deposit rate persistently above the base rate', and that raising it 'at least by as much as the base rate is raised is warranted'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 14 December 2021

HU.text: the one-week deposit rate was raised to 3.6%, 120 bp over the 2.40% base rate
HU.label: Budapest Business Journal (MTI), 'MNB raises 1-week depo rate by 30 bp to 3.6%', 16 Dec 2021

HU.text: the one-week deposit rate was raised by 20 bp to 4%, '160 bp over the base rate' (2.40%)
HU.label: Budapest Business Journal (MTI), 'MNB raises 1-week depo rate by 20 bp to 4%', 30 Dec 2021

HU.text: with the base rate raised from 2.40% to 2.90% from 26 Jan (overnight deposit rate 2.90%, overnight and one-week collateralised lending rates 4.90%), the Council said that 'the catching up of the base rate to the level of the one-week deposit rate is warranted', that 'the Bank will further tighten monetary conditions by raising also the one-week deposit rate', and that 'The MNB will continue to set the one-week deposit rate at weekly tenders and will stand ready to raise it further if necessary'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 25 January 2022

HU.text: after three weekly tenders at 4%, the one-week deposit rate was raised by 30 bp to 4.3%; 'The one-week deposit rate now stands 140 bp over the 2.9% base rate'; deputy governor Barnabás Virág said the MNB aims to change the one-week deposit rate once a month and that the base rate and the one-week deposit rate 'could converge in the course of the first half of the year'
HU.label: Budapest Business Journal (MTI), 'MNB raises 1-week depo rate 30 bp to 4.3%', 27 Jan 2022

HU.text: with the base rate raised from 2.90% to 3.40% from 23 Feb (overnight and one-week collateralised lending rates 5.40%), the Council deemed it necessary 'to continue the base rate tightening cycle on a monthly basis while gradually raising it to the level of the one-week deposit rate'; 'The MNB will continue to set the one-week deposit rate at weekly tenders and will stand ready to raise it further if necessary'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 22 February 2022

HU.text: the one-week deposit rate was raised by 30 bp to 4.6%; 'The one-week deposit rate now stands 120 bp over the 3.4% base rate'
HU.label: Budapest Business Journal (MTI), 'MNB raises 1-week depo rate by 30 bp to 4.6%', 24 Feb 2022

HU.text: after the outbreak of the war in Ukraine the one-week deposit rate was raised by 75 bp to 5.35%; 'The one-week deposit rate now stands 195 bp over the 3.4% base rate'
HU.label: Budapest Business Journal (MTI), 'MNB raises 1-week depo rate by 75 bp to 5.35%', 3 Mar 2022

HU.text: the Council 'did not discuss changing the base rate' (3.40%) but widened the interest rate corridor: it 'increased the overnight and the one-week collateralised lending rate by 100 basis points to 6.40 percent' (from 9 Mar); 'If necessary, the Bank stands ready to continue to respond quickly and flexibly to commodity and financial market risks arising from the rapidly changing environment by setting the one-week deposit rate'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 8 March 2022

HU.text: the one-week deposit rate was raised by 50 bp to 5.85%; 'The rate is 245 bp over the 3.4% base rate'
HU.label: Budapest Business Journal (MTI), 'MNB raises 1-week deposit rate by 50 bp to 5.85%', 10 Mar 2022

HU.text: with the base rate raised from 3.40% to 4.40% from 23 Mar (overnight deposit rate 4.40%, overnight and one-week collateralised lending rates 7.40%), the Council said that 'The base rate will gradually catch up to the level of the one-week deposit rate evolving in the coming months' and that 'The MNB will continue to set the one-week deposit rate at weekly tenders'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 22 March 2022

HU.text: the one-week deposit rate was raised by 30 bp to 6.15%, 175 bp over the 4.4% base rate
HU.label: Budapest Business Journal (MTI), 'MNB raises 1-week deposit rate 30 bp to 6.15%', 24 Mar 2022

HU.text: with the base rate raised from 4.40% to 5.40% from 27 Apr (overnight deposit rate 5.40%, overnight and one-week collateralised lending rates 8.40%), the Council said 'The MNB will continue to set the one-week deposit rate at weekly tenders; however, the central bank normally determines the one-week deposit rate on a monthly basis'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 26 April 2022

HU.text: the one-week deposit rate was raised by 30 bp to 6.45%, 105 bp over the 5.4% base rate
HU.label: Budapest Business Journal (MTI), 'MNB raises 1-week deposit rate 30 bp to 6.45%', 28 Apr 2022

HU.text: with the base rate raised from 5.40% to 5.90% from 1 Jun (overnight deposit rate 5.90%, overnight and one-week collateralised lending rates 8.90%), the Council repeated that 'the central bank normally determines the one-week deposit rate on a monthly basis' and that 'The base rate will gradually catch up to the level of the one-week deposit rate evolving in the coming months'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 31 May 2022

HU.text: the one-week deposit rate was raised by 30 bp to 6.75%, 85 bp over the 5.9% base rate
HU.label: Budapest Business Journal (MTI), 'MNB raises 1-week deposit rate 30 bp to 6.75%', 2 Jun 2022

HU.text: between monthly meetings the one-week deposit rate was raised by 50 bp to 7.25%, 135 bp over the 5.9% base rate, after 'the forint weakened close to 403 to the euro, a new historical low'
HU.label: Budapest Business Journal (MTI), 'MNB raises 1-week deposit rate 50 bp to 7.25%', 16 Jun 2022

HU.text: with the base rate raised by 185 bp from 5.90% to 7.75% from 29 Jun, the Council considered it 'necessary to close the gap between the base rate and the one-week deposit rate' and 'warranted to increase the one-week deposit rate to the level of the base rate at the weekly tender following the interest rate decision'; the corridor was reset to an overnight deposit rate of base rate minus 0.50 points (7.25%) and overnight and one-week collateralised lending rates of base rate plus 2.50 points (10.25%)
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 28 June 2022

HU.text: deputy governor Barnabás Virág said the bank was bringing the base rate and the 1-week deposit rate to the same level, but 'this convergence would not be complete, as the bank will continue to decide on the 1w depo rate every week and it will raise it if necessary'; 'If there is an unscheduled 1-week deposit rate hike, it will be included in the next monthly base rate hike'
HU.label: Portfolio, 'Hungary central banker says dual interest rate regime coming to an end', 28 Jun 2022

HU.text: at the Thursday tender the one-week deposit rate was raised by 50 bp to 7.75%, equal to the base rate (7.75% from 29 Jun), 'closing the spread between the two rates in line with its earlier pledge'
HU.label: Reuters via Lincoln Daily News, 'Hungary lifts key rate further on eye-watering inflation forecast', 30 Jun 2022

HU.text: with the base rate raised by 200 bp from 7.75% to 9.75% from 13 Jul (overnight deposit rate 9.25%, overnight and one-week collateralised lending rates 12.25%), the Council said 'it is warranted to raise the base rate to the level of the one-week deposit interest rate' (raised to 9.75% on 7 Jul), so the two rates are equal again
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 12 July 2022

HU.text: with the base rate raised by 100 bp from 9.75% to 10.75% from 27 Jul (overnight deposit rate 10.25%, overnight and one-week collateralised lending rates 13.25%), the Council said 'it is warranted to increase the interest rate on the one-week deposit instrument by the same measure as in the base rate'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 26 July 2022

HU.text: the one-week deposit rate was raised by 100 bp to 10.75%, 'keeping the rate in tandem with the base rate'
HU.label: Budapest Business Journal (MTI), 'MNB raises 1-week deposit rate by 100 bp to 10.75%', 28 Jul 2022

HU.text: with the base rate raised by 100 bp from 10.75% to 11.75% from 31 Aug (overnight deposit rate 11.25%, overnight and one-week collateralised lending rates 14.25%), the Council said 'it is warranted to increase the interest rate on the one-week deposit instrument by the same measure as in the base rate' and announced that 'The Bank will raise the required reserve ratio set for the banking system', hold discount bill auctions regularly and 'introduce a long-term deposit instrument'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 30 August 2022

HU.text: the one-week deposit rate was raised by 100 bp to 11.75%, 'keeping the rate in tandem with the base rate'
HU.label: Budapest Business Journal (MTI), 'MNB Raises 1-Week Deposit Rate by 100 bp to 11.75%', 1 Sep 2022

HU.text: with the base rate raised by 125 bp from 11.75% to 13.00% from 28 Sep (overnight deposit rate 12.50%, overnight and one-week collateralised lending rates 15.50%), the Council said 'it is warranted to increase the interest rate on the one-week deposit instrument by the same measure as in the base rate', that it 'has decided to stop the cycle of base rate hikes after the step in September', and that 'From October 1, the MNB will significantly reduce forint liquidity by raising the required reserve ratio, holding central bank discount bond auctions regularly and launching a longer-term deposit instrument'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 27 September 2022

HU.text: the one-week deposit rate was raised by 125 bp to 13%, 'keeping it in tandem with the base rate'
HU.label: Budapest Business Journal (MTI), 'MNB Raises 1-Week Deposit Rate to 13%, Level With Base Rate', 29 Sep 2022

HU.text: leaving the base rate at 13.0% and the overnight deposit rate at 12.5%, the Council 'raised the overnight collateralised lending rate to 25 percent and suspended the one-week collateralised loan, with effect from 8:45 a.m. on 14 October'; 'from 14 October 2022, the MNB will announce one-day (T/N) foreign exchange swap instrument and overnight (O/N) deposit quick tenders on a daily basis at higher interest rate levels than before'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council’s decision, effective from 8:45 a.m. on 14 October 2022

HU.text: 'Virág said the T/N FX swap instrument would be announced with a rate of 17% and the O/N deposit with a rate of 18%': the overnight deposit quick tender rate is 500 bp above the 13% base rate (the BIS series); 'The council left the base rate unchanged at 13%'
HU.label: Budapest Business Journal (MTI), 'MNB Raises O/N Collateralised Lending Rate by 950 bp to 25%', 14 Oct 2022

HU.text: banks placed HUF 1,549.22 billion 'at an interest of 18% in the central bank's one-day deposit quick tender' on 18 Oct; the first such tender on 14 Oct came 'when the MNB announced a 500-basis-point rate hike, as the interest at its tender the preceding day was still 13.0%'; 'Another emergency measure was to ditch the one-week deposit tender from the toolkit as of Monday, and now the MNB uses only the one-day deposit tenders to absorb liquidity'
HU.label: Portfolio, 'Hungary central bank one-day deposit quick tender breaks record', 19 Oct 2022

HU.text: the Council kept the base rate at 13.00%, the overnight deposit rate at 12.50% and the overnight collateralised lending rate at 25.00%, and said the MNB 'will continue to use the instruments introduced in mid-October as long as it is warranted by the maintenance of market stability and developments in risk perceptions'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 25 October 2022

HU.text: with the base rate (13%), the overnight deposit rate (12.5%) and the overnight repo rate (25%) unchanged, 'the effective rate will remain defined by the one-day deposit quick tender, which now sits at 18%'; Virág said a significant improvement in risk sentiment was needed 'to gradually reduce the spread between the base rate (13%) and the effective rate (18%)'
HU.label: ING Think, 'National Bank of Hungary Review: Financial and price stabilities in focus', 25 Oct 2022

HU.text: 'the benchmark rate since mid-October is the 18% one-day deposit rate, which is decided every morning by the central bank'; although in mid-October the quick tender was presented as a short-term measure, 'no change was applied to the tender ever since, with the rate remaining 18%'
HU.label: Portfolio, 'Hungary cenbank to hold policy meeting with very few open issues', 21 Nov 2022

HU.text: the Council kept the base rate at 13.00% (overnight deposit rate 12.50%, overnight collateralised lending rate 25.00%); 'The one-day deposit quick tenders and FX swap transactions result in tighter interest rate conditions at the short end of the yield curve', and the MNB 'will use its instruments introduced in mid-October until a trend improvement in risk perceptions occurs'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 22 November 2022

HU.text: 'the temporary and targeted measures, introduced in mid-October, will remain in place until there is a material and permanent improvement in the general risk sentiment'; ING expected the MNB to keep this set-up at its December meeting and to signal that more progress was needed before 'moving away from the 18% effective marginal rate (defined by the one-day deposit quick tender)'
HU.label: ING Think, 'National Bank of Hungary preview: Too early to quit', 14 Dec 2022

HU.text: the Council kept the base rate at 13.00%, the overnight deposit rate at 12.50% and the overnight collateralised lending rate at 25.00%; 'The targeted measures taken by the Bank in mid-October led to an improvement in financial market stability in a rapidly changing risk environment. The one-day deposit quick tenders and FX swap transactions result in tighter interest rate conditions at the short end of the yield curve', and the MNB 'will use its instruments introduced in mid-October until a trend improvement in risk perceptions occurs'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 20 December 2022

HU.text: 'no change in the regular overnight deposit rate at 12.50%, the base rate at 13% and the overnight repo rate at 25%': the 18% marginal rate (the one-day deposit quick tender) stays 500 bp over the base rate (the BIS series); 'The Monetary Council wants to see a trend improvement in risk perceptions, thus it adopts a patient approach' before it can 'start approaching the 18% marginal rate to the 13% base rate with gradual steps'
HU.label: ING Think, 'National Bank of Hungary Review: Keeping the gunpowder dry', 20 Dec 2022

HU.text: the Council kept the base rate at 13%, the overnight deposit rate at 12.5% and the overnight collateralised lending rate at 25%; 'the Bank will continue to use one-day deposit quick tenders and FX swap transactions to ensure financial market stability', and the MNB 'will maintain the current terms of its instruments introduced in mid-October until a trend improvement in risk perceptions occurs'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 24 January 2023

HU.text: 'The regular overnight deposit rate remained at 12.50%, the base rate at 13.00% and the overnight repo rate at 25.00%'; with the required reserve ratio to be doubled to 10%, liquidity 'will be pushed from the one-day quick deposit (now at 18%) to reserves (now at 13%, determined by the base rate)', which ING said lowers the probability that the MNB will 'prematurely reduce the effective marginal interest rate which stands at 18% now'
HU.label: ING Think, 'National Bank of Hungary review: Good things come to those who wait', 25 Jan 2023

HU.text: the Council kept the base rate at 13%, the overnight deposit rate at 12.5% and the overnight collateralised lending rate at 25%; 'the Bank will use one-day deposit quick tenders and FX swap transactions in the coming period in order to ensure financial market stability', optional reserves 'will be remunerated at the overnight quick deposit tender rate instead of the base rate', and 'the Bank takes into account the persistence of the recent improvement in risk perceptions when setting the conditions of overnight instruments introduced in mid-October'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 28 February 2023

HU.text: 'The regular overnight deposit rate remained at 12.50%, the base rate at 13.00% and the overnight repo rate at 25.00%'; in the reshaped reserve system optional reserves will earn 'the interest rate of the quick deposit tender (now at 18%)', 500 bp over the base rate (the BIS series)
HU.label: ING Think, 'National Bank of Hungary Review: Not fooled by promises, waiting for proof', 28 Feb 2023

HU.text: the Council kept the base rate at 13%, the overnight deposit rate at 12.5% and the overnight collateralised lending rate at 25%; 'the MNB will use one-day deposit quick tenders and FX swap transactions in the coming period in order to ensure financial market stability' and 'will continue to take into account persistent changes in risk perceptions when setting the conditions of overnight instruments introduced in mid-October'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 28 March 2023

HU.text: 'no change in the regular overnight deposit rate at 12.50%, the base rate at 13.00% and the overnight repo rate at 25.00%'; 'There was no signal at all regarding any hint of a potential pivot on the marginal effective rate, which still sits at 18%', 500 bp over the base rate (the BIS series)
HU.label: ING Think, 'Hungary’s central bank ain’t got no room for change', 28 Mar 2023

HU.text: with the base rate (13%) and the overnight deposit rate (12.5%) unchanged, the Council found it 'warranted to announce one-day deposit quick tenders and FX swap transactions at unchanged interest rate levels'; having 'widened the interest rate corridor substantially' on 14 October 2022, it 'decided to narrow the interest rate corridor', reducing the overnight collateralised lending rate from 25% to 20.5% with effect from the next day
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 25 April 2023

HU.text: the Council 'cut the overnight collateralised lending rate (top-end of rate corridor) by 450bp to 20.5%. However, other rates in the interest rate complex remained on hold'; 'Market stability is managed by the overnight tools (previously known as temporary, targeted tools), especially the quick deposit tender at an 18% interest rate', while 'the 13% base rate is still on permanent hold'
HU.label: ING Think, 'National Bank of Hungary Review: A new beginning without commitment', 25 Apr 2023

HU.text: with the base rate kept at 13%, the Council said 'the persistent improvement in risk perceptions has enabled the Bank to take additional steps towards the normalisation of the interest rate environment': it lowered the overnight collateralised lending rate by 100 bp to 19.5% and found it 'warranted to reduce the interest rate on the one-day quick deposit tenders and foreign exchange swap tenders by 100 basis points'; 'If the improvement in risk perceptions persists, the Bank will continue the gradual convergence of the interest rate conditions of one-day tenders to the base rate'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 23 May 2023

HU.text: 'The National Bank of Hungary cut the effective rate by 100bp to 17%': from the next day 'the interest rate of the overnight quick deposit tender will be lowered to 17%. This means a 100bp effective rate cut', leaving the effective rate 400 bp over the 13% base rate (the BIS series), and 'a cut in the base rate is firmly not on the table'
HU.label: ING Think, 'National Bank of Hungary Review: Normalisation seasoned with hawkishness', 23 May 2023

HU.text: with the base rate kept at 13%, 'the still favourable risk environment has enabled the Bank to continue the normalisation of the interest rate environment': the overnight collateralised lending rate was lowered by 100 bp to 18.5%, and 'it is also warranted to reduce the interest rate on the one-day quick deposit tenders and foreign exchange swap tenders by 100 basis points'; 'If the improvement in risk perceptions persists, the Bank will continue the gradual convergence of the interest rate conditions of one-day tenders to the base rate'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 20 June 2023

HU.text: from the next day 'the interest rate of the overnight quick deposit tender will be lowered to 16%. This means a 100bp effective rate cut', leaving the effective rate 300 bp over the 13% base rate (the BIS series); the top of the corridor was cut 'by 100bp to 18.5%', and 'ongoing easing remains a function of market stability'
HU.label: ING Think, 'National Bank of Hungary Review: Normalisation remains a function of market stability', 20 Jun 2023

HU.text: with the base rate kept at 13%, 'the still favourable risk environment has enabled the Bank to continue the normalisation of the interest rate environment at the previous pace': the overnight collateralised lending rate was lowered by 100 bp to 17.5% and the one-day quick deposit tender and FX swap tender rates were cut by 100 basis points; 'If the improvement in risk perceptions persists, the Bank will continue the gradual convergence of the interest rate conditions of one-day tenders to the base rate at the previous pace'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 25 July 2023

HU.text: from the next day 'the interest rate of the overnight quick deposit tender will be lowered to 15%. This means a 100bp effective rate cut', leaving the effective rate 200 bp over the 13% base rate (the BIS series); 'the main policy tools in this stage are the overnight tools, mainly the quick deposit facility which plays the role of the effective rate. Any decision regarding the base rate will come only after the convergence of the effective rate and the base rate'
HU.label: ING Think, 'National Bank of Hungary review: Sticking to the script', 25 Jul 2023

HU.text: with the base rate kept at 13%, 'The Monetary Council continued to normalise the interest rate environment at the previous pace in August': the overnight collateralised lending rate was lowered by 100 bp to 16.5% and the one-day quick deposit tender and FX swap tender rates were cut by 100 basis points; 'If the improvement in risk perceptions persists, the Bank will continue to close the gap between the interest rate conditions of one-day tenders and the base rate'
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 29 August 2023

HU.text: from the next day 'the interest rate on overnight quick deposit tender will be cut to 14%. This is an effective rate cut of 100bp', leaving the effective rate 100 bp over the 13% base rate (the BIS series); Deputy Governor Virág reiterated 'that monetary policy is entering a new phase of normalisation after the merger of the effective and base rates'
HU.label: ING Think, 'National Bank of Hungary review: Monetary policy to come off autopilot soon', 29 Aug 2023

HU.text: at a meeting where it 'did not discuss a change in the central bank base rate' (13%), the Council 'examined possible directions for simplifying the monetary policy toolkit, in this context the Council decided that excess reserves remunerate the base rate', from the start of the following month
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 12 September 2023

HU.text: with the base rate kept at 13%, 'With a decrease of 100 basis points in the effective interest rate, the Monetary Council concluded the normalisation of the extraordinary interest rate environment. Following today’s decision, the base rate will become the effective central bank interest rate'; 'the gap between the interest conditions of one-day deposit tenders and the base rate has closed', and 'the interest rate corridor became symmetric, with a band of +/- 100 basis points around the base rate' (overnight deposit rate 12.00%, overnight collateralised lending rate 14.00%); from the following month the reserve account is available 'without an upper limit', remunerated at the base rate; the base rate (the BIS series) is again the MNB's effective rate
HU.label: MNB, Press release on the Monetary Council meeting of 26 September 2023

HU.text: 'The base rate remained unchanged at 13%', and 'the central bank lowered the effective rate (the overnight quick deposit tender rate) by 100bp, bringing it to the same level as the base rate'; with the overnight quick deposit tender being phased out at the start of the following month, excess liquidity 'is expected to flow into the reserve account as excess reserves, where the interest rate is set by the base rate. This makes the reserve account as the main monetary policy instrument'
HU.label: ING Think, 'National Bank of Hungary review: Delivering the promise', 26 Sep 2023
